200.title: Poland Joins EU Satellite Project to Build European Alternative to Starlink
200.summary: Poland has joined an European Union initiative to create a secure satellite internet network designed as a European alternative to services such as Elon Musk’s Starlink.
200.body: Poland has joined an European Union initiative to create a secure satellite internet network designed as a European alternative to services such as Elon Musk’s Starlink. With its share of EU post-pandemic recover money, Warsaw will contribute €656 million (2.8 billion zloty) to the IRIS² program (Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity and Security by Satellite), a planned multi-orbit satellite internet constellation to be deployed by the European Union by 2027. The move comes as Poland seeks a larger role in Europe’s space sector, particularly as Warsaw has recently been selected to host a new European Space Agency security centre — the agency’s first facility outside its 11 founding member states.

300.title: Poland Inflation Confirmed at 3.0% in July
300.summary: News / Trading Economics / Poland Inflation Confirmed at 3.0% in July Poland Inflation Confirmed at 3.0% in July Less than 1 min read PLIRYY The annual inflation rate in Poland accelerated to 3.0% year-on-year in July 2026 from 2.5% in the previous month, confirming preliminary estimates. Inflation also accelerated for information and communication (5.2% vs 4.0%) and recreation, sport and culture (5.4% vs 5.2%).
300.body: News / Trading Economics / Poland Inflation Confirmed at 3.0% in July Poland Inflation Confirmed at 3.0% in July Less than 1 min read PLIRYY The annual inflation rate in Poland accelerated to 3.0% year-on-year in July 2026 from 2.5% in the previous month, confirming preliminary estimates. The pickup was mainly driven by faster price growth for transport (7.0% vs 1.3% in June), reflecting a sharp rebound in transport costs, and alcoholic beverages and tobacco (6.9% vs 6.5%). Inflation also accelerated for information and communication (5.2% vs 4.0%) and recreation, sport and culture (5.4% vs 5.2%). In contrast, prices continued to decline for clothing and footwear (-3.6% vs -3.1%), while inflation eased for housing and utilities (4.5% vs 4.9%), health (4.9% vs 5.0%), education services (5.3% vs 6.0%), and restaurants and accommodation services (4.2% vs 4.5%).

300.body: Poland's deputy minister said that without Ukrainians, the country's economy could come to a standstill Kyiv • UNN August 12 2026, 10:16 PM • 12795 views Polish Deputy Minister Maciej Duszczyk said that Ukrainians are filling the labor shortage and that without them the economy would have ground to a halt. Poland’s Deputy Minister of the Interior and Administration Maciej Duszczyk said that all Ukrainians stopping work in the country could effectively bring the Polish economy to a halt. If all Ukrainians united one day and did not go to work, the Polish economy would come to a standstill - Duszczyk said. Duszczyk criticized the idea of deporting unemployed Ukrainians The deputy minister also criticized the proposal by the Law and Justice party to deport unemployed Ukrainian men of conscription age from Poland.
